interpretation: The gain comes from reversing what is reused: precompute the prime set P once and translate it by consecutive primes q_i near the interval base, so many tests of whether e-q_i is prime become the monotone coverage process F_{i+1}=F_i union (P+q_{i+1}). This exchanges generation of every prime in each high interval for a larger reusable set of smaller primes plus only k nearby primes. The uniform-density calculation merely suggests a workable k; an interval is established only when the actual union covers every even target. Because existence of some decomposition suffices, the method gains reuse while giving up control over whether the returned prime summand is extremal.
